subject: Rounded shares that add up to one: apportion in stats, used by share and pivot
brief:
Make rounded shares in tabula add up, in three places that follow one rule.

1. A new function `apportion(values, digits)` in the stats module: each value's share of the total, rounded to `digits` decimal places so that the rounded shares add up to exactly 1. Rounding each share on its own is not acceptable (three equal values would each be rounded down and add up to less than 1). The rule is largest remainder: first cut every share down to `digits` decimals; the units of the last decimal place still missing to reach 1 are then given out one each to the shares that lost the most in that cut; when two shares lost the same amount, the one at the earlier position gets the unit. Compute this exactly, so that floating-point error never decides a tie, and return each share as a float rounded to `digits`. None stays None in its place and counts as 0. Edge case: when the total is 0, every position is None. Every other value must be a number of at least 0 (booleans are not numbers); anything else raises ValueError, as does a `digits` that is not a whole number of at least 0.
2. `share` in the window module uses this rule whenever `digits` is given (without digits nothing changes, negative values included). It also takes `by` (one column name or a list): shares are then relative to the total of the rows with the same `by` values, the results stay in the table's row order, and with digits each group's shares add up to 1. An empty `by` list raises ValueError, an unknown column KeyError.
3. `pivot` takes `normalize` (None by default, `rows` or `all`) and `digits`. With `rows` every cell becomes its share of its own row's total; with `all`, its share of the total of all cells, apportioned over the cells in row-major order (so ties go to the earlier row, then to the earlier column). Cells whose aggregate is None count as 0 and stay None; cells that have no matching rows count as 0 and keep `fill`. With digits the rounding follows apportion; without it the shares are plain divisions. Any other normalize value raises ValueError, and so does digits without normalize.

All behavior that the existing tests check must keep working.
